thread:
tj: FYI saw a spike in backend fetches during tenant handoff yesterday. appears to be read amplification caused by aggressive demotes on shared prefixes. anyone else observed similar?

maria: saw noisy metrics too around 03:12 UTC. sample trace would help - are these small prefixes or large keyspaces?

tj: smallish prefixes (~4k keys) but hot. when we demote quickly across nodes the coalescer loses hits and we see a cascade of misses. pasted a tiny trace:```
rpc: ReadBatch(keys=4) -> hit prefixes {A,B}
evict: demote prefix A (evict_ok)
ReadBatch: prefix A missed -> offpath fetch -> latency spike
```

kai: ugh. classic demote-against-batch problem but here it's churn from sharing heuristics. current eviction only looks at recency score. maybe need a mechanism to absorb quick flip-flops.

tj: thought: "eviction credits" - lightweight ephemeral tokens assigned per-prefix when they survive a demote window. each demote consumes a credit; if credits>0 we defer the demote and decrement credit. credits replenish slowly on stable accesses.

maria: interesting. so credits act as short-term hysteresis to prevent oscillation. how is this different from existing grace windows?

kai: grace windows are time-based only and global; credits can be consumed per-demote and provide a budgeted allowance for churn. they make the policy reactive to frequency rather than absolute time.

sophia: implementation notes: per-prefix {credits:int, last_replenish_ts}. increment credits on steady hits (token bucket style). eviction path checks credits>0 -> decrement + skip. credits capped to avoid long-term pinning.

tj: stress tradeoffs: extra per-prefix state (4 bytes per prefix?) vs avoiding N backend RPCs. likely worth it for hot shared prefixes.

maria: failures: if node restarts we lose credits -> could cause short burst of extra demotes. acceptable if credits are ephemeral. we should not persist them.

kai: need global fairness guard: a malicious tenant could hog credits and prevent eviction of cold prefixes elsewhere if credits are global. enforce per-tenant credit quota and per-node global cap.

sophia: also tie credits to demote cost estimate. large-prefix demotes cost more (IO) so consume more credits to discourage frequent demotes there. small prefixes consume 1 credit.

tj: metrics: credit_consumed, credit_replenished, demote_deferred, per-prefix credit_balance. those will tell us if settings are sane.

maria: testing: unit test for token-bucket replenish semantics, property test for churn scenarios. integration: simulate N tenants migrating hotness every 100ms and observe backend fetch rate.

kai: one more: integrate with prefetch/pin API. prefetch ops should be allowed to borrow credits (mark as borrower) but repay quicker. else prefetches get starved.

sophia: rollout plan: feature flag on node, enable for subset of shards. start with conservative caps: max 3 credits per prefix, replenish rate 1 credit / 5s.

ops-bot: canary plan registered at infra/canary/eviction-credits - 2% shards for 24h, capture metrics: backend_miss_rate, demote_deferrals, memory_use, credit_imbalance.

maria: sounds good. who will author short RFC addendum? include fallback steps and knob defaults.

tj: I will. reviewers: @kai, @sophia, @maria. will include benchmarks and flagged rollout.

kai: +1. please ensure global budget enforcement is in the first patch to avoid accidental starvation.

sophia: small nit: encode credits as u8 to keep maps compact. default caps tuned later.

maria: agreed. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
